newsitem.title: FRANCE: 10 detained in Corsican extortion case.
newsitem.headline: 10 detained in Corsican extortion case.

text.p: Police said on Wednesday they had detained 10 people for questioning in Corsica in connection with a bombing and an alleged extortion scheme at a golf course on the French Mediterranean island in December.
Three of those in custody were suspected of being intermediaries in the alleged scheme to extort protection money from the golf course owner by bombing it, police said.
Such payments are known in Corsica as a "revolutionary tax" demanded by separatists engaged in a two decade old campaign for increased autonomy from mainland France.
A top leader of the political wing of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), Francois Santoni, was already in custody in connection with the scheme, the police said.
In a related development, a bomb planted by suspected Corsican separatists destroyed a home in the town of Cargese in the south of the Mediterranean island, but caused no injuries, police said.
No one immediately claimed responsibility for the blast on Tuesday night. The owners of the building were away on holiday at the time.
Separatist bombings are virtually an everyday occurence on the resort island.
Economic difficulties have also brought conflict to Corsica.
Police clashed with angry farmers in the port of Bastia overnight in an unsuccessful effort to free the Danielle Casanova, a state-owned car ferry operating between Corsica and the mainland.
About a hundred farmers protesting at difficult economic conditions had occupied the ferry on Tuesday morning to prevent it from leaving port in protest at island economic difficulties.

But they later agreed to free the boat, saying they wanted to avoid further violence. They had initially insisted they would maintain their vigil until the government sent an emissary from Paris to negotiate with them.
